record.original_question: For primitive binary BCH codes of length 2^m−1, determine the exact minimum-distance behavior in the remaining unresolved case m = 12 discussed by the chapter.

evidence.quote: By using Newton identities they proved that two such codes have true minimum distance δ + 2. These are the BCH codes with designed distance 59 and 61. At the moment the case m = 12 remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m=12$ and $n=2^{m}-1=4095$. For a designed distance $\delta$ with $2\le \delta\le n$, the narrow-sense primitive binary BCH code $\mathrm{BCH}(n,\delta)$ of length $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is defined as the cyclic code whose generator polynomial is the least common multiple of the minimal polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of $\alpha,\alpha^{2},\ldots,\alpha^{\delta-1}$, where $\alpha$ is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_{2^{m}}$. By the BCH bound, the true minimum Hamming distance $d(\mathrm{BCH}(n,\delta))$ satisfies $d(\mathrm{BCH}(n,\delta))\ge \delta$. For odd designed distances $\delta$ that are not attained as Bose distances (so-called "non-narrow-sense gap" cases), determining whether $d(\mathrm{BCH}(n,\delta))=\delta$ or $d(\mathrm{BCH}(n,\delta))=\delta+2$ is of interest.

Determine the true minimum distance of the narrow-sense primitive binary BCH codes of length $n=4095$ in the remaining unresolved cases for $m=12$; in particular, decide for each such designed distance $\delta$ whether $d(\mathrm{BCH}(4095,\delta))$ equals $\delta$ or $\delta+2$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the true minimum distance of primitive binary BCH codes of length 4095 in the unresolved m = 12 case. Recent works (e.g., arXiv:2604.23594 and related papers from 2024–2025) continue to study minimum distances of narrow-sense primitive BCH codes, and the literature consistently characterizes the exact determination of these minimum distances as a long-standing hard problem with no comprehensive resolution. Status remains unclear from available evidence.

status_evidence.title: On the Minimum Distances of Some Families of BCH Codes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2026) study of minimum distances of further families of BCH codes, indicating ongoing research.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the true minimum distance of primitive BCH codes remains an active and largely open research area.

status_evidence.title: The Bose and Minimum Distance of a Class of BCH Codes
status_evidence.snippet: Determination of the minimum distance of BCH codes is of great interest, but is a very challenging problem with few theoretical results in the last four decades.
status_evidence.claim: The minimum-distance problem for primitive binary BCH codes is widely regarded as open in many cases.

status_evidence.title: On the minimum distance of a class of binary BCH codes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) paper continuing to resolve specific subfamilies of binary BCH code minimum distances.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work resolves additional cases but does not appear to settle the full m=12 case.
